answer: Graph-based trust propagation resists Sybil attacks by bounding score percolation across bottleneck cuts in interaction networks. Inside a verified agent garden, an attacker cannot funnel reputation into an isolated lagoon of fake peers; sustaining each branching willow of synthetic identities requires scarce endorsements from honest seeds, imposing prohibitive relationship capital costs. However, this topology heavily penalizes honest, newly deployed agents through severe cold-start friction.
